title: Singers in bands and Bob Lyons's band
summary: Punch says musicians rarely sang, credits Louis Dumaine with first singing blues on trumpet, and lists Bob Lyons's men.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I see Now what about vocalists in those days? Who did they have that sang in a band? Well I'm going to tell you something Dick If you're talking about here

The musicians wasn't doing much singing in bands Now like Tuxedo they had a girl singin' Who was that? Oh the girl played the piano What name was Jeanette? No Camilla, wasn't it? Camilla Todd Yeah, she did a little singin'
And he come along though, he come along because I'll tell ya, who was it?

Some man got up and started singing the blues, a trumpet player, I don't know who you were now, in Bob Lyons band, he played trumpet and he sung the blues and after that where everybody's trumpet player started singing. Who could that been anyhow? Let me see what Bob used to have with him. Boy used to write music, what did he name, not Mad Cat, he used to play with him. You know this boy, he ain't been dead long. Lewis Dumaine, yeah. He played with, he wasn't playing steady with Bob, but he worked a few jobs with him. Who did Bob have in his band there while we were? Because he was playing trombone, he was playing trombone, Willie Connish, Willie Connish, and Lurens of Stahl on guitar. They didn't use but five pieces. No piano. No piano. No saxophone. No saxophone. No saxophone. No saxophone. Tuxedo band, the only band used a piano. And they have a piano when they go to a place to play. But I mean like on the streets they didn't use no piano.
